record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every chiral polytope K with regular facets admit a chiral extension whose Schläfli symbol has any prescribed last entry?

evidence.quote: Problem 25 Does every chiral polytope K with regular facets admit a chiral extension with prescribed last entry of the Schlafli symbol?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a ranked partially ordered set (with faces of ranks $-1, 0, 1, \dots, n$, including a unique minimum face of rank $-1$ and a unique maximum face of rank $n$) satisfying the standard diamond, flag-connectivity, and strong flag-connectivity axioms; its facets are the faces of rank $n-1$. The Schläfli symbol of such a polytope (when it is well-defined) is the tuple $\{p_1, p_2, \dots, p_{n-1}\}$, where $p_i$ is the number of $i$-faces in any section of rank $2$ formed by an $(i-2)$-face and an $(i+1)$-face. A polytope is called regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on its flags. It is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits (so the polytope has full rotational symmetry but admits no reflection-like symmetry). 

Given an abstract polytope $\mathcal{K}$ of rank $n-1$, a polytope $\mathcal{P}$ of rank $n$ is called an extension of $\mathcal{K}$ if every facet of $\mathcal{P}$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{K}$. It is known that if $\mathcal{K}$ is chiral with regular facets and has Schläfli symbol $\{p_1, \dots, p_{n-2}\}$, then any chiral extension $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathcal{K}$ has Schläfli symbol of the form $\{p_1, \dots, p_{n-2}, q\}$ for some integer $q \geq 3$.

Problem. Does every chiral polytope $\mathcal{K}$ with regular facets admit, for every prescribed integer $q \geq 3$ (or more generally, for every admissible value $q$), a chiral extension whose Schläfli symbol has last entry equal to $q$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been partially addressed. Constructions exist showing that certain chiral polytopes with regular facets admit chiral extensions whose Schläfli symbol has arbitrarily large last entry (e.g., extensions where the last entry is lcm(2s, q) for a parameter s, and constructions for chiral toroids). However, the general statement—that every chiral polytope with regular facets admits a chiral extension with any prescribed last entry of the Schläfli symbol—does not appear to be fully established.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes (arXiv:2003.02933)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of chiral extensions of certain chiral polytopes are introduced such that the last entry of the Schläfli symbol is arbitrarily large.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: chiral extensions with arbitrarily large last Schläfli entry are constructed for certain chiral polytopes with regular facets, not all.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Extensions of Regular Toroids
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs chiral extensions of regular toroids and discusses control over the Schläfli symbol.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on the prescribed-last-entry question for specific families.
